document_check.note: Zhang X, Lan X, Chen C, Ren H, Guo Y. 'Effects of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in Patients With Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.' Front Hum Neurosci 2021;15:723715. The cited numbers match: SMD 0.83 (95% CI 0.44 to 1.22), I² = 65%, 12 studies, 329 patients; global-cognition subgroup of nine studies (271 patients), I² = 71%.

cited_result: The pooled standardised mean difference for rTMS versus sham on cognitive function in MCI (SMD 0.83, 95% CI 0.44 to 1.22, I² 65%, 12 RCTs, 329 patients), with the global-cognition subgroup (nine trials, I² 71%) as the secondary cited figure.
tool_reason: The cited result is the pooled effect estimate of a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials, so ROBIS applies.

domains.rationale: The review was registered in PROSPERO and the eligibility criteria (RCTs, MCI by any criteria, rTMS versus sham, cognitive outcomes) fit the question. Minor issues: the 'severe degree of cognitive impairment' exclusion is vague, and conference reports were excluded without justification. The registration identifier's year prefix (CRD42021...) suggests registration after the stated March 2020 search date, so prospective registration is uncertain, but no deviation is reported.

signalling.question: 1.1 Did the review adhere to pre-defined objectives and eligibility criteria?
signalling.quote: (http://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/; registration number: CRD 42021238708)

signalling.question: 1.2 Were the eligibility criteria appropriate for the review question?
signalling.quote: (2) participants diagnosed with MCI based on any diagnostic criteria ... (4) the control group received sham rTMS stimulation

signalling.question: 1.3 Were eligibility criteria unambiguous?
signalling.quote: (b) severe degree of cognitive impairment

signalling.question: 1.4 Were all restrictions in eligibility criteria based on study characteristics appropriate?
signalling.quote: (e) studies that did not have sham stimulation as the control group

signalling.question: 1.5 Were any restrictions in eligibility criteria based on sources of information appropriate?
signalling.quote: (c) articles were reviews or conference reports

domains.domain: Domain 2: Identification and selection of studies
domains.rationale: The search was broad: eight English and Chinese databases plus reference lists, though no trial registries. But the stated search cut-off ('published before March 11, 2020') conflicts with the inclusion of Yuan et al. (2021). The selection flow does not reconcile: 922 records assessed, 873 excluded at title and abstract, 58 excluded at full text, and 12 included, which is 21 more than the records available. Independent duplicate screening is not explicitly stated.

signalling.question: 2.1 Did the search include an appropriate range of databases/electronic sources for published and unpublished reports?
signalling.quote: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Chinese Technical Periodicals (VIP), Wanfang Database, and China BioMedical Literature Database (SinoMed)

signalling.question: 2.2 Were methods additional to database searching used to identify relevant reports?
signalling.quote: The reference lists of identiﬁed articles were manually searched to select other potential studies.

signalling.question: 2.3 Were the terms and structure of the search strategy likely to retrieve as many eligible studies as possible?
signalling.quote: (“Cognitive Dysfunction” OR “mild cognitive impairment” OR “MCI”) AND (“Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation” OR “TMS” OR “repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation” OR “rTMS”)

signalling.question: 2.4 Were restrictions based on date, publication format, or language appropriate?
signalling.quote: The following databases were searched to identify studies published before March 11, 2020 [no language restriction stated; but Table 1 includes 'Yuan et al. (2021)', p. 6, which contradicts this cut-off]

signalling.question: 2.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in selection of studies?
signalling.quote: XZ and XL were responsible for the literature screening and data extraction. [flow, p. 6: 'A total of 873 studies were excluded after reading their titles and abstracts. In addition, 58 articles were excluded after full-text reading.' These counts do not reconcile with 922 records and 12 inclusions.]

domains.domain: Domain 3: Data collection and study appraisal
domains.rationale: Extraction and risk-of-bias assessment were done in duplicate with the Cochrane tool, and study characteristics are tabulated. However, there is no rule for which of a trial's several cognitive measures entered the main pooled analysis ('All outcome indicators ... were combined'). The correlation coefficient used to impute change-score SDs is not stated.

signalling.question: 3.1 Were efforts made to minimise error in data collection?
signalling.quote: Two researchers working independently examined and extracted data from the selected studies.

signalling.question: 3.2 Were sufficient study characteristics available for both review authors and readers to be able to interpret the results?
signalling.quote: TABLE 1 | Characteristics of studies included in the meta-analysis.

signalling.question: 3.3 Were all relevant study results collected for use in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: All outcome indicators used for the evaluation of cognitive function in all trials were combined.

signalling.question: 3.4 Was risk of bias (or methodological quality) formally assessed using appropriate criteria?
signalling.quote: The risk of bias was assessed using methods recommended by the Cochrane Collaboration Network (Cumpston et al., 2019)

signalling.question: 3.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in risk of bias assessment?
signalling.quote: Two researchers (LXY and CCJ) independently extracted data from each included study and compared the results.

domains.rationale: The main SMD pools different cognitive constructs (global, memory, executive) and protocols from 1 to 40 sessions. Three crossover trials are included without any stated handling: arm totals of 182 + 178 = 360 exceed the 329 patients, which suggests crossover participants were counted in both arms. Change-score SDs were imputed with an unstated correlation. Only one sensitivity analysis was done, dropping one study from a subgroup. Risk of bias was not built into the synthesis: all trials were called 'mild risk' although only two reported adequate concealment. Publication-bias test results are not reported. Subgroup differences were interpreted without interaction tests.

signalling.question: 4.1 Did the synthesis include all studies that it should?
signalling.quote: This meta-analysis included 12 RCT studies with a total of 329 patients with MCI.

signalling.question: 4.2 Were all pre-defined analyses reported or departures explained?
signalling.quote: Searched for protocol-specified analyses and reported departures; the review lists four subgroup analyses (p. 4) and mentions a sensitivity analysis only in the Results (p. 8), but the registered protocol's analyses are not described.

signalling.question: 4.3 Was the synthesis appropriate given the nature and similarity in the research questions, study designs and outcomes across included studies?
signalling.quote: A random-eﬀects model was used due to the considerable variability in the methods used to evaluate outcome indicators. ... The number of participants randomly assigned to the active rTMS group was 182, while those randomly assigned to the sham rTMS group were 178.

signalling.question: 4.4 Was between-study variation (heterogeneity) minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: moderate between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 65%, Figure 4). Subgroup analyses were performed to determine variables that may inﬂuence cognitive function outcomes.

signalling.question: 4.5 Were the findings robust, e.g. as demonstrated through funnel plot or sensitivity analyses?
signalling.quote: Sensitivity analyses were also performed, and one study with a low SD (Cui et al., 2019), which did not signiﬁcantly inﬂuence the combined SMD was omitted.

signalling.question: 4.6 Were biases in primary studies minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: Two studies reported allocation procedures with adequate concealment. Further, most studies were double-blind to both subjects and evaluators. Therefore, all included studies were considered to have a mild risk of bias (Figure 3).

domains.domain: Phase 3: Risk of bias in the review
domains.rationale: The limitations section acknowledges small numbers and heterogeneous parameters. Even so, the conclusions call rTMS 'safe and effective' and treat subgroup contrasts as established. They do not temper the pooled estimate for the Domain 2 to 4 concerns: the crossover handling, the pooling of mixed outcomes, the largely unclear allocation concealment, and the absence of robustness analyses.

signalling.question: A. Did the interpretation of findings address all of the concerns identified in Domains 1 to 4?
signalling.quote: Overall, this meta-analysis reveals that rTMS is a safe and eﬀective non-invasive neural modulation tool in MCI

signalling.question: B. Was the relevance of identified studies to the review's research question appropriately considered?
signalling.quote: The outcome indicators in the rTMS group were compared with those of the control group, which received sham rTMS only.

signalling.question: C. Did the reviewers avoid emphasising results on the basis of their statistical significance?
signalling.quote: The results suggested that long-term rTMS treatment substantially improved cognitive function more strongly than short-term rTMS treatment.

overall_rationale: Domain 4 is high concern and Domains 2 and 3 are unclear. The interpretation does not address these concerns, so the ROBIS overall rating is High. The main problems are pooling heterogeneous cognitive constructs, apparent double-counting of crossover participants, unstated imputation assumptions, no sensitivity analysis on the main estimate, primary-study bias not addressed in the synthesis, and inconsistencies in the search dates and selection counts.
